title: Typing | U.S. State Facts
description: Learn more about each of the 50 U.S. states while honing your typing skills! Recommended for students who have already completed one of our introductory typing courses that covers home row, top row, and bottom row.

lessons.name: Welcome!
lessons.text1: Get ready to type all about the 50 great states of the USA!

instruction.body: Before starting this course, you should complete a TypingClub course that covers the basics! We'll be typing a variety of letters, numbers, and symbols on the keyboard.

lessons.name: USA
lessons.text1: The United States of America, or USA, is a country in North America. There are 50 states in the USA.

lessons.name: States
lessons.text1: We'll type about state capitals, abbreviations, symbols, and fun facts! Let's get started.

lessons.name: USA
lessons.text1: There are 50 states in the United States of America. The United States is a huge country with regions that can be very different from one another.

lessons.name: Alaska & Hawaii
lessons.text1: Alaska and Hawaii are the westernmost states of the USA. They are not connected by land to the other 48 states.

lessons.name: Hawaii
lessons.text1: Hawaii is made up of several volcanic islands in the Pacific Ocean.

lessons.name: Alaska 1
lessons.text1: Alaska is much farther north. It has islands in the Pacific Ocean too, but a large part of it is connected to mainland Canada.

lessons.name: West Coast 1
lessons.text1: The west coast of the mainland United States is made up of Washington, Oregon, and California.

lessons.name: West Coast Game
lessons.text1: Alaska Hawaii Washington Oregon California

lessons.name: Northwest
lessons.text1: The northern part of the West Coast is sometimes called the Pacific Northwest.

lessons.name: The West
lessons.text1: The other Western states are Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Wyoming, Utah, Colorado, Arizona, and New Mexico.

lessons.name: The West Game
lessons.text1: Western states Idaho Montana Nevada Wyoming Utah Colorado Arizona New Mexico

lessons.name: The Southwest
lessons.text1: Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of the states that border them, California, Nevada, Utah, Colorado, and Texas, are the American Southwest.

lessons.name: The Southwest Game
lessons.text1: Arizona New Mexico California Nevada Utah Colorado Texas

lessons.name: The Great Lakes
lessons.text1: There are more midwestern states that border the Great Lakes. These are Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio.

lessons.name: The Great Lakes Game
lessons.text1: Minnesota Wisconsin Michigan Illinois Indiana Ohio

lessons.name: The Midwest
lessons.text1: Inland from the West is the Midwest, which includes the states of North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Iowa, and Missouri.

lessons.name: South Central
lessons.text1: The South Central part of the United States includes Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Arkansas.

lessons.name: Midwest & South Central Game
lessons.text1: North Dakota South Dakota Nebraska Kansas Iowa Missouri Texas Oklahoma Louisiana Arkansas

lessons.name: Southeast
lessons.text1: The states of the Southeast are Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Kentucky, and Tennessee.

lessons.name: Southeast Game
lessons.text1: Florida Alabama Mississippi Georgia North Carolina South Carolina Kentucky Tennessee Virginia West Virginia Maryland Delaware

lessons.name: The Mid-Atlantic
lessons.text1: The mid-Atlantic states are Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and New York.

lessons.name: D.C.
lessons.text1: Washington, D.C. is also located in the mid-Atlantic. Washington, D.C. is the capital city of the United States. D.C. stands for District of Columbia, a special area that is not a state.

lessons.name: Northeast
lessons.text1: New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania are also considered part of the Northeast.

lessons.name: New England
lessons.text1: The rest of the Northeast is New England, which is Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Vermont, Rhode Island, and Connecticut.

lessons.name: Northeast Game
lessons.text1: Pennsylvania New Jersey New York Maine Massachusetts New Hampshire Vermont Rhode Island Connecticut

lessons.name: States
lessons.text1: Some states belong to more than one region because they are on the border or because the land or culture of the state is a mix.

lessons.name: Your State
lessons.text1: What region or regions is your state in? What is the land and culture like where you live?

lessons.name: Non-contiguous states
lessons.text1: Alaska and Hawaii are considered non-contiguous states because they are not connected by land to the other 48 states.

lessons.name: AK
lessons.text1: The capital of Alaska is Juneau and its abbreviation is AK. It is known for its glaciers and vast wilderness.

lessons.name: AK Symbols
lessons.text1: Alaska's state flower is the forget-me-not, and its bird is the willow ptarmigan.

lessons.name: AK Facts
lessons.text1: On January 3, 1959, Alaska became the 49th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Last Frontier." As of 2022, its population is 0.733 million.

lessons.name: AK Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Alaska has more coastline than the other 49 states combined.

lessons.name: AK Game
lessons.text1: Juneau willow ptarmigan AK Alaska forget me not glaciers

lessons.name: HI
lessons.text1: The capital of Hawaii is Honolulu, and its abbreviation is HI. It's known for its beautiful beaches and volcanic landscapes.

lessons.name: HI Symbols
lessons.text1: Hawaii's state flower is the hibiscus, and its bird is the nene.

lessons.name: HI Facts
lessons.text1: On August 21, 1959, Hawaii became the 50th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Aloha State." As of 2022, its population is 1.441 million.

lessons.name: HI Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Hawaii is the only U.S. state made up entirely of islands.

lessons.name: HI Game
lessons.text1: Honolulu nene HI Hawaii hibiscus volcanoes

lessons.name: West Coast
lessons.text1: The West Coast states are Washington, Oregon, and California. Let's learn more about each state!

lessons.name: CA
lessons.text1: The capital of California is Sacramento, and its abbreviation is CA. It is known for its diverse culture and iconic landmarks like Hollywood.

lessons.name: CA Symbols
lessons.text1: California's state flower is the golden poppy, and its bird is the California valley quail.

lessons.name: CA Facts
lessons.text1: On September 9, 1850, California became the 31st state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Golden State." As of 2022, its population is 39.029 million.

lessons.name: CA Fun Fact
lessons.text1: California produces more than 80% of the world's almonds.

lessons.name: CA Game
lessons.text1: Sacramento golden poppy valley quail Hollywood California

lessons.name: OR
lessons.text1: The capital of Oregon is Salem, and its abbreviation is OR. It is known for its forests and rugged coastline.

lessons.name: OR Symbols
lessons.text1: Oregon's state flower is the Oregon grape, and its bird is the western meadowlark.

lessons.name: OR Facts
lessons.text1: On February 14, 1859, Oregon became the 33rd state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Beaver State." As of 2022, its population is 4.27 million.

lessons.name: OR Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Oregon is the only state with a two-sided flag, featuring a beaver on the reverse.

lessons.name: OR Game
lessons.text1: Salem Oregon grape western meadowlark beaver coastline

lessons.name: WA
lessons.text1: The capital of Washington is Olympia, and its abbreviation is WA. It is known for its rainforests and tech industry.

lessons.name: WA Symbols
lessons.text1: Washington's state flower is the western rhododendron, and its bird is the willow goldfinch.

lessons.name: WA Facts
lessons.text1: On November 11, 1889, Washington became the 42nd state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Evergreen State." As of 2022, its population is 7.738 million.

lessons.name: WA Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Washington state is the largest producer of apples in the U.S.

lessons.name: WA Game
lessons.text1: Olympia Washington WA western rhododendron willow goldfinch rainforests

lessons.name: Western States
lessons.text1: The Western states are Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Wyoming, Utah, Colorado, Arizona, and New Mexico.

lessons.name: ID
lessons.text1: Boise is the capital of Idaho, and its abbreviation is ID.

lessons.name: ID Symbols
lessons.text1: Idaho's state flower is the syringa, and its bird is the mountain bluebird.

lessons.name: ID Facts
lessons.text1: On July 3, 1890, Idaho became the 43rd state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Gem State." As of 2022, its population is 1.996 million.

lessons.name: ID Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Idaho produces about one-third of the potatoes grown in the U.S.

lessons.name: ID Game
lessons.text1: Boise Idaho ID gems potatoes syringa mountain bluebird

lessons.name: MT
lessons.text1: The capital of Montana is Helena, and its abbreviation is MT.

lessons.name: MT Symbols
lessons.text1: Montana's state flower is the bitterroot, and its bird is the western meadowlark.

lessons.name: MT Facts
lessons.text1: On November 8, 1889, Montana became the 41st state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Treasure State." As of 2022, its population is 1.144 million.

lessons.name: MT Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Montana has more cattle than people.

lessons.name: MT Game
lessons.text1: Helena Montana MT western meadowlark bitterroot treasure

lessons.name: NV
lessons.text1: The capital of Nevada is Carson City, and its abbreviation is NV. It is known for its deserts and the city of Las Vegas.

lessons.name: NV Symbols
lessons.text1: Nevada's state flower is the sagebrush, and its bird is the mountain bluebird.

lessons.name: NV Facts
lessons.text1: On October 31, 1864, Nevada became the 36th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Silver State." As of 2022, its population is 3.225 million.

lessons.name: NV Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Nevada is the driest state in the U.S., receiving less than 10 inches of rain annually.

lessons.name: NV Game
lessons.text1: Carson City Nevada NV Las Vegas sagebrush mountain bluebird

lessons.name: CO
lessons.text1: The capital of Colorado is Denver, and its abbreviation is CO. It is known for the Rocky Mountains and outdoor recreational activities.

lessons.name: CO Symbols
lessons.text1: Colorado's state flower is the Rocky Mountain columbine, and its bird is the lark bunting.

lessons.name: CO Facts
lessons.text1: On August 1, 1876, Colorado became the 38th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Centennial State." As of 2022, its population is 5.839 million.

lessons.name: CO Fun Facts
lessons.text1: Colorado has the highest mean altitude of any state.

lessons.name: CO Game
lessons.text1: Denver Colorado CO Rocky Mountain columbine lark bunting

lessons.name: WY
lessons.text1: The capital of Wyoming is Cheyenne, and its abbreviation is WY. It is known for its wide-open spaces and Yellowstone National Park.

lessons.name: WY Symbols
lessons.text1: Wyoming's state flower is the Indian paintbrush, and its bird is the western meadowlark.

lessons.name: WY Facts
lessons.text1: On July 10, 1890, Wyoming became the 44th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Equality State." As of 2022, its population is 0.579 million.

lessons.name: WY Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Wyoming was the first state to grant women the right to vote, in 1869.

lessons.name: WY Game
lessons.text1: Cheyenne Wyoming WY Indian paintbrush Western meadowlark Yellowstone

lessons.name: UT
lessons.text1: The capital of Utah is Salt Lake City, and its abbreviation is UT. It is known for its Mormon heritage and the Great Salt Lake.

lessons.name: UT Symbols
lessons.text1: Utah's state flower is the sego lily, and its bird is the California gull.

lessons.name: UT Facts
lessons.text1: On January 4, 1896, Utah became the 45th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Beehive State." As of 2022, its population is 3.421 million.

lessons.name: UT Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Utah is home to the Great Salt Lake, the largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere.

lessons.name: UT Game
lessons.text1: Salt Lake City Utah UT sego lily California gull Great Salt Lake

lessons.name: The Southwest
lessons.text1: Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of the states that border them, California, Nevada, Utah, Colorado, and Texas, are the American Southwest.

lessons.name: AZ
lessons.text1: The capital of Arizona is Phoenix, and its abbreviation is AZ. It is known for the Grand Canyon and desert landscapes.

lessons.name: AZ Symbols
lessons.text1: Arizona's state flower is the saguaro cactus blossom, and its bird is the cactus wren.

lessons.name: AZ Facts
lessons.text1: On February 14, 1912, Arizona became the 48th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Grand Canyon State." As of 2022, its population is 7.359 million.

lessons.name: AZ Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Arizona is home to the Grand Canyon, one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World.

lessons.name: AZ Game
lessons.text1: Phoenix Arizona AZ saguaro cactus blossom cactus wren Grand Canyon

lessons.name: NM
lessons.text1: The capital of New Mexico is Santa Fe, and its abbreviation is NM. It is known for its desert landscapes and Pueblo-style architecture.

lessons.name: NM Symbols
lessons.text1: New Mexico's state flower is the yucca, and its bird is the greater roadrunner.

lessons.name: NM Facts
lessons.text1: On January 6, 1912, New Mexico became the 47th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Land of Enchantment." As of 2022, its population is 2.113 million.

lessons.name: NM Fun Fact
lessons.text1: New Mexico has the highest percentage of Hispanic and Native American populations of any U.S. state.

lessons.name: NM Game
lessons.text1: Santa Fe New Mexico NM yucca greater roadrunner Pueblo

lessons.name: The Midwest
lessons.text1: Inland from the West is the Midwest, which includes the states of North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Iowa, and Missouri.

lessons.name: NE
lessons.text1: The capital of Nebraska is Lincoln, and its abbreviation is NE. It is known for its prairies and pioneer history.

lessons.name: NE Symbols
lessons.text1: Nebraska's state flower is the goldenrod, and its bird is the western meadowlark.

lessons.name: NE Facts
lessons.text1: On March 1, 1867, Nebraska became the 37th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Cornhusker State." As of 2022, its population is 1.988 million.

lessons.name: NE Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Nebraska's Chimney Rock was a major landmark for pioneers on the Oregon Trail.

lessons.name: NE Game
lessons.text1: Lincoln Nebraska NE goldenrod western meadowlark Chimney Rock

lessons.name: ND
lessons.text1: The capital of North Dakota is Bismarck, and its abbreviation is ND. It is known for its Great Plains and Badlands.

lessons.name: ND Symbols
lessons.text1: North Dakota's state flower is the wild prairie rose, and its bird is the western meadowlark.

lessons.name: ND Facts
lessons.text1: On November 2, 1889, North Dakota became the 39th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Peace Garden State." As of 2022, its population is 0.787 million.

lessons.name: ND Fun Fact
lessons.text1: North Dakota is home to the geographic center of North America.

lessons.name: ND Game
lessons.text1: Bismarck North Dakota ND western meadowlark wild prairie rose

lessons.name: SD
lessons.text1: The capital of South Dakota is Pierre, and its abbreviation is SD. It is known for Mount Rushmore and the Black Hills.

lessons.name: SD Symbols
lessons.text1: South Dakota's state flower is the pasque flower, and its bird is the ring-necked pheasant.

lessons.name: SD Facts
lessons.text1: On November 2, 1889, South Dakota became the 40th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Mount Rushmore State." As of 2022, its population is 0.925 million.

lessons.name: SD Fun Fact
lessons.text1: South Dakota is home to Mount Rushmore, featuring the faces of four U.S. presidents.

lessons.name: SD Game
lessons.text1: Pierre South Dakota SD Mount Rushmore pasque flower pheasant

lessons.name: IA
lessons.text1: The capital of Iowa is Des Moines, and its abbreviation is IA. It is known for its agriculture and the Iowa State Fair.

lessons.name: IA Symbols
lessons.text1: Iowa's state flower is the wild rose, and its bird is the eastern goldfinch.

lessons.name: IA Facts
lessons.text1: On December 28, 1846, Iowa became the 29th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Hawkeye State." As of 2022, its population is 3.2 million.

lessons.name: IA Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Iowa is the only state whose east and west borders are formed entirely by rivers.

lessons.name: IA Game
lessons.text1: Des Moines Iowa IA wild rose eastern goldfinch rivers state fair

lessons.name: KS
lessons.text1: The capital of Kansas is Topeka, and its abbreviation is KS. It is known for its prairies and tornado activity.

lessons.name: KS Symbols
lessons.text1: Kansas' state flower is the native sunflower, and its bird is the western meadowlark.

lessons.name: KS Facts
lessons.text1: On January 29, 1861, Kansas became the 34th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Sunflower State." As of 2022, its population is 2.937 million.

lessons.name: KS Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Kansas is known as the Sunflower State, but it also produces the most wheat in the U.S.

lessons.name: KS Game
lessons.text1: Topeka Kansas KS native sunflower western meadowlark

lessons.name: MO
lessons.text1: The capital of Missouri is Jefferson City, and its abbreviation is MO. It is known for the Gateway Arch and the Ozarks.

lessons.name: MO Symbols
lessons.text1: Missouri's state flower is the hawthorn, and its bird is the bluebird.

lessons.name: MO Facts
lessons.text1: On August 10, 1821, Missouri became the 24th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Show-Me State." As of 2022, its population is 6.178 million.

lessons.name: MO Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Missouri is home to the country's first public university, the University of Missouri, established in 1839.

lessons.name: MO Game
lessons.text1: Jefferson City Missouri MO hawthorn bluebird Gateway Arch university

lessons.name: The Great Lakes
lessons.text1: There are more midwestern states that border the Great Lakes. These are Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio.

lessons.name: IL
lessons.text1: The capital of Illinois is Springfield, and its abbreviation is IL. It is known for its farmland and as the home of Abraham Lincoln.

lessons.name: IL Symbols
lessons.text1: Illinois' state flower is the violet, and its bird is the northern cardinal.

lessons.name: IL Facts
lessons.text1: On December 3, 1818, Illinois became the 21st state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Prairie State." As of 2022, its population is 12.582 million.

lessons.name: IL Fun Fact
lessons.text1: The first McDonald's was opened in Des Plaines, Illinois, in 1955.

lessons.name: IL Game
lessons.text1: Springfield Illinois IL violet northern cardinal prairie Abraham Lincoln

lessons.name: IN
lessons.text1: The capital of Indiana is Indianapolis, and its abbreviation is IN. It is known for the Indianapolis 500 auto race.

lessons.name: IN Symbols
lessons.text1: Indiana's state flower is the peony, and its bird is the northern cardinal.

lessons.name: IN Facts
lessons.text1: On December 11, 1816, Indiana became the 19th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Hoosier State." As of 2022, its population is 6.833 million.

lessons.name: IN Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Indiana is home to the Indianapolis 500, the largest single-day sporting event in the world.

lessons.name: IN Game
lessons.text1: Indianapolis Indiana IN peony northern cardinal Indianapolis 500 car race

lessons.name: MI
lessons.text1: The capital of Michigan is Lansing, and its abbreviation is MI. It is known for the Great Lakes and automobile industry.

lessons.name: MI Symbols
lessons.text1: Michigan's state flower is the apple blossom, and its bird is the American robin.

lessons.name: MI Facts
lessons.text1: On January 26, 1837, Michigan became the 26th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Great Lakes State." As of 2022, its population is 10.034 million.

lessons.name: MI Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Michigan has more lighthouses than any other state.

lessons.name: MI Game
lessons.text1: Lansing Michigan MI apple blossom American robin lighthouses Great Lakes

lessons.name: MN
lessons.text1: The capital of Minnesota is Saint Paul, and its abbreviation is MN. It is known for its lakes and cold winters.

lessons.name: MN Symbols
lessons.text1: Minnesota's state flower is the pink and white lady slipper, and its bird is the common loon.

lessons.name: MN Facts
lessons.text1: On May 11, 1858, Minnesota became the 32nd state in the Union. Its nickname is "The North Star State." As of 2022, its population is 5.715 million.

lessons.name: MN Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Minnesota is known as the "Land of 10,000 Lakes," but it actually has over 11,800 lakes.

lessons.name: MN Game
lessons.text1: Saint Paul Minnesota MN pink and white lady's slipper common loon

lessons.name: OH
lessons.text1: The capital of Ohio is Columbus, and its abbreviation is OH. It is known for its role in aviation history and as the "Birthplace of Aviation."

lessons.name: OH Symbols
lessons.text1: Ohio's state flower is the scarlet carnation, and its bird is the northern cardinal.

lessons.name: OH Facts
lessons.text1: On March 1, 1803, Ohio became the 17th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Buckeye State." As of 2022, its population is 11.78 million.

lessons.name: OH Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Ohio is known as the "Mother of Presidents," as it is the birthplace of seven U.S. presidents.

lessons.name: OH Game
lessons.text1: Columbus Ohio OH carnation northern cardinal presidents aviation

lessons.name: WI
lessons.text1: The capital of Wisconsin is Madison, and its abbreviation is WI. It is known for its dairy production and Great Lakes shoreline.

lessons.name: WI Symbols
lessons.text1: Wisconsin's state flower is the wood violet, and its bird is the American robin.

lessons.name: WI Facts
lessons.text1: On May 29, 1848, Wisconsin became the 30th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Badger State." As of 2022, its population is 5.892 million.

lessons.name: WI Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Wisconsin produces more cheese than any other state.

lessons.name: WI Game
lessons.text1: Madison Wisconsin WI wood violet American robin cheese badger

lessons.name: South Central
lessons.text1: The South Central part of the United States includes Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Arkansas.

lessons.name: AR
lessons.text1: The capital of Arkansas is Little Rock, and its abbreviation is AR. It is known for its natural beauty and hot springs.

lessons.name: AR Symbols
lessons.text1: Arkansas' state flower is the apple blossom, and its bird is the mockingbird.

lessons.name: AR Facts
lessons.text1: On June 15, 1836, Arkansas became the 25th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Natural State." As of 2022, its population is 3.041 million.

lessons.name: AR Fun Fact
lessons.text1: The only active diamond mine in the U.S. is in Murfreesboro, Arkansas.

lessons.name: AR Game
lessons.text1: Little Rock Arkansas AR apple blossom mockingbird diamonds natural

lessons.name: LA
lessons.text1: The capital of Louisiana is Baton Rouge, and its abbreviation is LA. It is known for its vibrant culture and Mardi Gras celebrations.

lessons.name: LA Symbols
lessons.text1: Louisiana's state flower is the magnolia, and its bird is the eastern brown pelican.

lessons.name: LA Facts
lessons.text1: On April 30, 1812, Louisiana became the 18th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Pelican State." As of 2022, its population is 4.623 million.

lessons.name: LA Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Louisiana has the tallest state capitol building in the U.S. at 450 feet.

lessons.name: LA Game
lessons.text1: Baton Rouge Louisiana LA magnolia brown pelican New Orleans

lessons.name: OK
lessons.text1: The capital of Oklahoma is Oklahoma City, and its abbreviation is OK. It is known for its oil production and Native American heritage.

lessons.name: OK Symbols
lessons.text1: Oklahoma's state flower is the Oklahoma rose, and its bird is the scissor-tailed flycatcher.

lessons.name: OK Facts
lessons.text1: On November 16, 1907, Oklahoma became the 46th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Sooner State." As of 2022, its population is 4.007 million.

lessons.name: OK Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Oklahoma has the largest population of Native Americans in the U.S.

lessons.name: OK Game
lessons.text1: Oklahoma City Oklahoma OK Oklahoma rose scissor tailed flycatcher

lessons.name: TX
lessons.text1: The capital of Texas is Austin, and its abbreviation is TX. It is known for its large size and diverse culture.

lessons.name: TX Symbols
lessons.text1: Texas's state flower is the bluebonnet, and its bird is the northern mockingbird.

lessons.name: TX Facts
lessons.text1: On December 29, 1845, Texas became the 28th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Lone Star State." As of 2022, its population is 30.345 million.

lessons.name: TX Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Texas is the only state to have been an independent nation before joining the U.S.

lessons.name: TX Game
lessons.text1: Austin Texas TX bluebonnet northern mockingbird Lone Star State

lessons.name: Southeast
lessons.text1: The states of the Southeast are Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Kentucky, and Tennessee.

lessons.name: AL
lessons.text1: The capital of Alabama is Montgomery, and its abbreviation is AL. It is known for its rich history in the Civil Rights Movement.

lessons.name: AL Symbols
lessons.text1: Alabama's state flower is the camellia, and its bird is the yellowhammer.

lessons.name: AL Facts
lessons.text1: On December 14, 1819, Alabama became the 22nd state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Yellowhammer State." As of 2022, its population is 5.074 million.

lessons.name: AL Fun Fact
lessons.text1: The first 911 call in the U.S. was made in Haleyville, Alabama, in 1968.

lessons.name: AL Game
lessons.text1: Montgomery Alabama AL camellia northern flicker yellowhammer civil rights

lessons.name: FL
lessons.text1: The capital of Florida is Tallahassee, and its abbreviation is FL. It is known for its beaches and theme parks like Walt Disney World.

lessons.name: FL Symbols
lessons.text1: Florida's state flower is the orange blossom, and its bird is the mockingbird.

lessons.name: FL Facts
lessons.text1: On March 3, 1845, Florida became the 27th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Sunshine State." As of 2022, its population is 22.244 million.

lessons.name: FL Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Florida is the flattest state in the U.S., with the highest point being only 345 feet above sea level.

lessons.name: FL Game
lessons.text1: Tallahassee Florida FL orange blossom northern mockingbird sunshine beaches Disney World

lessons.name: GA
lessons.text1: The capital of Georgia is Atlanta, and its abbreviation is GA. It is known for its peaches and as a major transportation hub.

lessons.name: GA Symbols
lessons.text1: Georgia's state flower is the Cherokee rose, and its bird is the brown thrasher.

lessons.name: GA Facts
lessons.text1: On January 2, 1788, Georgia became the 4th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Peach State." As of 2022, its population is 10.9 million.

lessons.name: GA Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Georgia is known as the Peach State, but it's also the largest producer of pecans in the U.S.

lessons.name: GA Game
lessons.text1: Atlanta Georgia GA Cherokee rose brown thrasher Peach State

lessons.name: KY
lessons.text1: The capital of Kentucky is Frankfort, and its abbreviation is KY. It is known for the Kentucky Derby.

lessons.name: KY Symbols
lessons.text1: Kentucky's state flower is the goldenrod, and its bird is the northern cardinal.

lessons.name: KY Facts
lessons.text1: On June 1, 1792, Kentucky became the 15th state in the Union. Its nickname is "The Bluegrass State." As of 2022, its population is 4.512 million.

lessons.name: KY Fun Fact
lessons.text1: Kentucky is the home of the Kentucky Derby, the oldest continuously held horse race in the U.S.

lessons.name: KY Game
